answer: An agent network can make voting power depend on a refundable stake locked for each identity, while capping how quickly new accounts gain influence. If an account is caught duplicating identities to evade the cap, its stake is slashed and its reputation reset. This does not make Sybils impossible; it makes influence costly: an attacker must lock up capital across accounts and risk losing it. A saffron, vine, or juniper label may distinguish agents, but labels alone cannot establish unique identity.
